hints.title: Bidirectional Friendship Mapping
hints.text: Unify friendships in both directions so that each user lists all their immediate friends.

hints.title: Joining Pages Liked by Friends
hints.text: Join each user friends with the likes table to discover pages endorsed by their social network.

hints.title: Excluding Self-Liked Pages
hints.text: Filter out pages the user has already liked themselves, grouping by user and page to count friend likes.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllFriends AS (
    SELECT user1_id AS user_id, user2_id AS friend_id FROM Friendship
    UNION
    SELECT user2_id AS user_id, user1_id AS friend_id FROM Friendship
)
SELECT
    f.user_id,
    l.page_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT f.friend_id) AS friends_likes
FROM AllFriends f
JOIN Likes l ON f.friend_id = l.user_id
LEFT JOIN Likes self ON f.user_id = self.user_id AND l.page_id = self.page_id
WHERE self.page_id IS NULL
GROUP BY f.user_id, l.page_id;
```

complexity.time: O(F * L) where F is friendships and L is likes
complexity.space: O(F + L) working memory for join buckets
complexity.notes: Symmetric friendship graph traversal with anti-join exclusion.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per user page recommendation recompute friendship sets repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: UNION deduplication ensures bidirectional friendship symmetry.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle bidirectional graph representation and exclude already-liked pages.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def recommend_page(friendship: pd.DataFrame, likes: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    f1 = friendship.rename(columns={"user1_id": "user_id", "user2_id": "friend_id"})
    f2 = friendship.rename(columns={"user2_id": "user_id", "user1_id": "friend_id"})
    all_friends = pd.concat([f1, f2]).drop_duplicates()
    
    friend_likes = all_friends.merge(likes, left_on="friend_id", right_on="user_id", suffixes=("", "_like"))
    self_likes = set(zip(likes["user_id"], likes["page_id"]))
    
    recs = friend_likes[~friend_likes.apply(lambda r: (r["user_id"], r["page_id"]) in self_likes, axis=1)]
    res = recs.groupby(["user_id", "page_id"])["friend_id"].nunique().reset_index()
    return res.rename(columns={"friend_id": "friends_likes"})
solutions.approach: Symmetric merge and self-like exclusion in pandas
